page: Microsoft Azure DC1s_v3 is a single-core virtual machine belonging to the DCSv3 server family. It is equipped with one dedicated physical core and one vCPU powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, featuring 48 KB of L1d cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache. It includes 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per core ratio. There is no local storage bundled with this instance, though it is Premium Storage capable, and it does not feature a GPU.

Performance benchmarks reflect its single-core configuration. The instance achieves average tier results in single-threaded operations, with a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 1875.88 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1628.0. Single-threaded gzip compression reaches 28.27 GB/sec, and bzip3 decompression performs at 10.48 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics fall into the lower percentiles due to the single-vCPU limitation, with a Passmark CPU score of 2253.06 and a static web serving throughput of 2.76 GB/sec. Redis SET operations perform at 2.14 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the DC1s_v3 offers a dedicated CPU allocation and a high memory-to-core ratio of 1:8, making it a viable entry-level option for workloads requiring dedicated execution resources without the overhead of multi-core pricing. It is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded applications, basic database operations, small-scale web serving, or development and testing environments that require Intel Xeon architecture features like AVX-512 and cryptography acceleration.
